paper.title: A strategy of win-stay, lose-shift that outperforms tit-for-tat in the Prisoner's Dilemma game

headline: Nowak-Sigmund 1993 WSLS/Pavlov (noisy IPD, agent-based): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; WSLS self-play=2.95 vs TFT self-play=2.25 under noise; WSLS-vs-ALLC=3.96; co-evolving cooperative-regime late WSLS freq=0.98 (> TFT 0.02); ALLC dies under WSLS (0.00) but takes over under TFT (1.00)

verdicts.gate: P1 two WSLS restore cooperation under noise: WSLS self-play ≥ 2.7 AND WSLS_self − TFT_self ≥ 0.5
P2 WSLS exploits ALLC: WSLS-vs-ALLC ≥ 4.5 AND ≥ TFT-vs-ALLC + 1.0
reasons: WSLS-vs-ALLC = 3.9650 (need ≥ 4.5); TFT-vs-ALLC = 3.0094; margin = 0.9556 (need ≥ 1.0). Faithful memory-one WSLS=(1,0,0,1) vs ALLC locks into EITHER CC(R=3) or DC(T=5) — noise moves it symmetrically between them, so its mean sits at ~(R+T)/2 = 4.0, honestly short of the ≥4.5 bar.

verdicts.gate: P3 WSLS dominates the co-evolving noisy population: late WSLS freq ≥ 0.5 and > TFT AND WSLS resists ALLC invasion while TFT admits it

extra.distinctness: NOT the noise-free deterministic Axelrod round-robin (where TFT wins). WSLS beats TFT specifically because of NOISE (error-correction of accidental defections) + EVOLUTION (exploitation of drifting ALLC). The gate is a noisy evolving population, not the static tournament.
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published game-theoretic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + locked-prediction discipline reproduce WSLS's noise+evolution advantage over TFT and would catch an artifact

citations: Nowak, M. & Sigmund, K. (1993). A strategy of win-stay, lose-shift that outperforms tit-for-tat in the Prisoner's Dilemma game. Nature 364:56-58. doi:10.1038/364056a0.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against exact Markov pairwise payoffs + a finite-population evolutionary + invasion experiment. The sibling axelrod_ipd (deterministic noise-free tournament, TFT wins) is the DISTINCTNESS contrast, not a numeric baseline
